mechanism: the three quantisation levels are supervised separately on their own soft assignments: level 1 aggregates the edges the frozen AF3 curvature calls locally dense, measured with the contract's Poincare kernel; level 2 refines inside the level-1 group; level 3 keeps related items distinguishable; a balance term keeps every level's mean assignment near uniform

calls.name: the curved agreement kernel of one pair
calls.note: exp(-d_H / temperature) with the contract's Poincare distance. This is the explicit curve operation of the level-1 term.

calls.name: the level-1 term of one pair
calls.note: -w * log K, where w is the AF3 weight of the edge. The behaviour signal and the curve are on the same path: setting w to zero removes the term and moving the curvature changes K.

calls.name: the overlap of two soft assignments
calls.note: sum_k a_k b_k, the probability mass the two items put on the same code. Level 2 refines on this overlap inside the level-1 group and level 3 caps it for related items.

coupling.note: The behaviour signal is the training graph's AF3 curvature, which weights each edge; the curve is the contract Poincare kernel of the two items' expected level-1 codewords. Both are multiplied on the same path into the level-1 term, so zeroing the AF3 weight removes the term and moving the curvature changes it.

excluded.reason: the baseline's balanced assignment decides the identifiers; the mechanism only reads the residuals and the codebooks through a soft read-out
a frozen per-edge constant read from the table exported by the issue-#136 convention; it carries no gradient
a clip of an affine function of a constant; piecewise linear and flat outside the ramp, exercised by the arm's own tests
a read-only statistic of the step's gradient norms, measured with autograd.grad and never differentiated through

excluded.reason: discrete index selections driven by the current argmax assignment; they choose which pairs the terms see and carry no gradient
